finding.claim: Unvalidated SSRF in /preview: attacker-supplied url query parameter is fetched server-side with requests.get and the status code plus first 500 bytes of the body are returned to the caller.

trace.note: target read from attacker-controlled query parameter url
target passed unmodified to requests.get; no scheme, host, IP, or redirect validation
status_code and resp.text[:500] returned to attacker (full-response SSRF)

finding.guards_checked: None on path. requests only supports http/https adapters, so file:// and gopher:// are rejected by the library; this is not a guard in the code. Internal http targets (169.254.169.254, localhost, RFC1918) are reachable.

verdict.guard_found: none. The /preview handler (app.py:13-17) has no host, scheme, or IP check before requests.get at app.py:16. The ALLOWED_HOSTS check at app.py:23-24 guards only the separate /partner route, not /preview.
verdict.reason: The url query parameter is read at app.py:15 with no authentication on the route, passed unvalidated to requests.get at app.py:16, and the status code and first 500 bytes of the response are returned at app.py:17, so an unauthenticated attacker can reach internal http targets through /preview.

finding.claim: Allowlist bypass via redirect in /partner: hostname allowlist is checked only on the initial URL, but requests.get follows redirects by default, so an allowlisted partner host returning a 3xx to an internal address is fetched. Only the status code is returned.

trace.note: target read from attacker-controlled query parameter url
host checked against ALLOWED_HOSTS (api.partner.example, cdn.partner.example); rejects others with 400
requests.get(target) follows redirects by default; a redirect from an allowlisted host to an internal IP is fetched without re-validation
status_code returned (status-only oracle for internal hosts)

finding.guards_checked: Hostname allowlist at app.py:9 and app.py:24 (validates only the first hop, not redirect targets). No allow_redirects=False. No resolved-IP check. Exploitability depends on an allowlisted partner host having an open redirect or being attacker-influenced.

verdict.guard_found: Only the first-hop hostname check at app.py:24 (ALLOWED_HOSTS membership on urlparse(target).hostname). No allow_redirects=False on the requests.get at app.py:26, no resolved-IP or redirect-target validation. Not a closing guard because it validates only the initial URL.
verdict.reason: The source at app.py:22 is attacker-controlled, the hostname check at app.py:24 covers only the first hop, and requests.get at app.py:26 follows redirects by default, so an allowlisted host's 3xx to an internal address is fetched and its status returned at app.py:27. Exploitation still requires an allowlisted partner host that redirects to an attacker-chosen or internal target, which is a precondition outside this code.

finding.claim: Parser differential in /partner (unverified candidate): the allowlist parses the URL with urlparse (app.py:23) but the unmodified string is fetched with requests/urllib3 (app.py:26); userinfo/backslash variants such as http://169.254.169.254\@api.partner.example/ may pass the check while the fetch targets the internal IP.

trace.note: hostname derived via urlparse (CPython urlsplit: netloc ends at /, ?, #; backslash not a delimiter)
raw target string handed to requests/urllib3, which parses it independently; divergence unverified

finding.guards_checked: Allowlist at app.py:24-25 uses a different parser than the fetch. Not executed: Python execution was blocked in this sandbox and urllib3 is not installed locally, so the divergence was not confirmed.

verdict.guard_found: app.py:23-25: `host = urlparse(target).hostname` followed by `if host not in ALLOWED_HOSTS` (exact set membership on the parsed hostname), which returns 400 before the fetch at app.py:26.
verdict.reason: The trace lines match the code (app.py:22, 23, 26) and `url` is attacker-controlled, but exact set membership on the parsed hostname at app.py:24-25 is a closing guard under the rubric, so the finding is refuted. The parser-differential bypass (e.g. backslash userinfo) is unverified because urllib3 could not be run here, and a real bypass would need to be shown separately.
